cards.name: Open Letter
cards.content:
No End of Beginnings

 

In this first open letter you will find an audio recording of and reflection on the memorial for Grace Alderwood, news of our two-year-old daughter and four month old son, a report on our family's general well-being and my professional journey, as well as hints about adventures into which I hope to find my way in the not-so-distant future. I hope you will interpret what you find here as an invitation to reflect, comment, offer challenges, ask for more information, and become involved, either with me or more deeeply in your own work to meet your needs while helping to make the world a more just and peaceful community.

 

{{OL01img01|size:large;float:right}} This first proper letter is a bit long (and the following ones will be shorter) because it gets the metaphorical starch, yeast, and hops together and lights the fire under something I've been brewing for a very long time. I didn't like the pressure of writing my dissertation, but I loved the research and writing itself. It became clear to me that I can quite happily spend hours in a room by myself, pouring over texts and thinking about what I've read in order to share it with other people. This practice creates a kind of pressure, not only to create text of my own that I hope will be understood by others but also to put the written word to some use through thinking with other people about how we think, feel, and perform in co-creating our world. I feel compelled to explore, write, and teach or perform. My life is a bit busy right now, but I can't wait any longer before allowing my mixture to ferment, so I'll be tending it every day in private and tempting others to share samples of the product with some regularity. I designed and will continue to develop the Culturesmith website in order to do this work. Please make sure you subscribe to my email reminders using the box in the right margin of this window under the words "Enter your email address." You may also click on the gear icon at the upper right of this (or any) card and select "follow".

 

Part of this letter is behind a password on my website because it is also time to practice what I've preached for my entire adult life and keep more current with people who want to connect on a deeper level and who make up my community, near and far. Several folks have asked to be kept up-to-date by email on the more personal aspects of our Ups and Downs, especially during this time of transition. It turns out that sending anything by email or Facebook, or whatever new device of social media, has largely come to be considered the same as releasing it to the entire world with implicit permission that it may be used as anyone sees fit. I've decided to be more circumspect and not to release to the general public any more detail about our more problematic dilemmas than is necessary. If you have signed in, and continue to read past this point, you hereby agreed to keep what you read behind the log-in confidential. Please contact me if you need to change that agreement at any time and for any reason. I appreciate your understanding.

 

Outreach

 

Writing

{{Towards Beginnings image|size:medium;float:right}}I'd like to invite you to consider reading the first article of mine published since earning the Ph.D. It is [[Bluevolution|also located on this website]], both in sections and as a whole in PDF format. If you can afford to [[https://gumroad.com/l/Anqd|purchase the article]] (for only $4) or [[http://www.amazon.com/Towards-Beginnings-Images-Edition-Volume/dp/1481281402/ref=sr_1_4?ie=UTF8&qid=1356195705&sr=8-4&keywords=Towards+Beginnings+Images+of+end|the entire journal]], by all means please do.

 

Free Aiki

As founder and Chief Instructor of [[Free Aiki Dojo]] I continue to offer free aikido classes (pay-what-you-can or PWYC when possible) from four to six times a week, thanks in large part to the generosity of my host and teacher, [[Amber Arvidsson]] of [[Aikido of Berkeley]], and our non-profit [[Association Building Community]].

 

Golden Bears Aikido at UC Berkeley

I accepted an invitation from students at UC Berkeley to be Chief Instructor for aikido on the Cal campus and helped them reinstate the organization there begun by Senseis [[Margaret Falconer]] and [[Douglas Chamberlain]] in 1968. With the members of the community who make up Free Aiki Dojo, all of my students are welcome to train together both on and off campus and also often attend Madeline Thurston's classes at Aikido of Berkeley. [[http://goldenbearsaikido.com|Golden Bears Aikido]] has also added new sempai, named Rob Pierce, to the teaching roster. He promptly began a late night Thursday class on-campus which will resume with the school year. Opportuities to grow on campus continue to present themselves, and we would deeply appreciate any help you might offer in that area. People discover that I really do mean that anyone is invited to train no matter their financial situation, and have begin donating training uniforms (gi and hakama) as well as the time required to circulate PR materials. 

 

The Aikido Archives at Sofia University

It continues to be my great good fortune to have been invited by Margaret Falconer Sensei, founder of the Institute for Transpersonal Psychology now known as [[Sofia University]], to create (design with [[Ethan McCutchen]] of Grass Commons' Wagn.org) and curate the [[Aikido Archives]] at that institution. We will launch publicly in the coming months and welcome the creative input of members of the global aikido commmunity among our guest curators and contributors.

 

Martial Concordance

{{OL01img02|size:large;float:right}}In the Summer of 2011, I became the aikido and [[Martial Concordance]] (MNv) instructor at The Renaissance School in Oakland. Since then, I introduced and have been developing my [[Peace Practices]] (PcPx) curriculum for use by the whole learning community, including students, staff, faculty and parents. Lori Bridgewater, Head of School at and owner of TRS, is an enthusiastic supporter of the work in which over fifty children and adults from TRS have participated so far, and has invited me to teach the staff, make public presentations. I introduce the Peace Practices curriculum to adults through public demonstrations during which I describe the aikido and MNv classes in progress now, ask parents of children who are in the program to speak, introduce the [[Peace Practices]] curriculum under consideration for the future, and take questions. To explain what this entails, I need your permission to sound a bit like a brochure for a few more seconds.

 

{{Martial Concordance+image|size:medium;float:right}}Martial Concordance® refers to a unique training and conflict facilitation method [[Jessup Patrick|I]] created which combines practices and concepts from the martial ([[aikido]]), theatrical (improv), and [[process arts]] (group facilitation) to prepare practitioners to provide co-creative leadership in the midst of conflict and during the process of systemic revision. Capable of engaging both obviously physical conflict and covert systemic violence, the adult practitioner becomes an artist working with group inquiry and long-term analysis, striving for the redefinition of peace itself as "conflict done well".®

[[http://culturesmith.com/Aikido_and_Attention|My article about Aikido and Attention issues]].

[[https://www.facebook.com/MartialNonviolence?fref=ts|MNv on Facebook]]


{{ConflictWell logo figures01framed|size:medium;float:right}}Peace Practices® is what I call MNv when it is wrapped into a unique curriculum designed for a specific group which wishes to transform into a community practicing peace on a daily basis. Here is the [[http://www.causes.com/causes/100237-peace-practices-whole-community-martial-concordance-training|Peace Practices page on Causes]] with much more information and video.

 

The remainder of this letter includes writing about a hero of mine, named Grace Alderwood, an audio recording of her memorial service, reports on challenges faced in getting Peace Practices off the ground, reflections on practicing what I preach, and a brief exploration of the gifts and pressures of family and vocation. If you do not see more in-depth content below this line, please sign in or request an account.

 

 {{OL01membercontent}}

 

 

 

If you are signed in, previous letters will appear below. If you are seeking older content, please look here.

{{Beginning Email 20130122|closed}}

 

Comments on previous letters will be found appended to those cards. This comment area is for the current issue and, if you are signed in, you will see a box below for the further addition of your thoughts. Please contribute in any way that feels right to you, including making suggestions and proposing corrections.

  --[[Jessup Patrick]]

Riley,

 

Thank you for generously sharing of your thoughts, experiences, stories. Variations on some of your themes are running through my life, so much resonance. This is the year of the snake, and a time for shedding worn out ways of moving through the world... whether we want to or not, they're coming off! Sometimes it can be a ripping sensation. In my experience, lately situations are arising which are there to give me information - it may not be the information that I want, but knowledge is always useful. I sometimes question whether to resist what seems to be unjust, or to simply engage more strongly with positive situations... or both. Like any piece of art, designing our lives depends on so many factors, preferences, choices; and is a constantly evolving process. I always enjoy reading about your journey; life isn't always comfortable, but the most difficult situations also make the best stories. The salon sounds like a great idea!

 

Be well,

Dhyana

--[[Dhyana Iris]].....2013-07-05 16:23:46 +0000

cards.name: OL01membercontent
cards.content:
Practicing What I Preach

I gave a demonstration last Fall after which a mother became so enthusiastic that she went looking for me out in the world to get me to teach her daughters independently. She went to the wrong dojo by mistake and a senior aikido instructor, who will remain nameless for the time being, took her aside and made several disparaging remarks about me personally, about my wife, Rowan, about my ability as an aikido instructor, and presented an opinion, thankfully entirely unsupported by fact or the opinion of any other human being, that I would likely harm her children should the parent allow me to teach them. The parent immediately related the conversation to Lori Bridgewater, the owner and TRS Head of school, and removed her children from my then upcoming classes, which immediately stopped along with the majority of my income, pending a criminal background check and a full investigation, both of which I recommended upon being notified of the issue by the school.

Lori Bridgewater attempted to contact the source of the slander four times, before being allowed to speak, and received only denials of any involvement and instructions to leave the premises. I have sent an open-ended "there must have been a mistake" letter, drafted language as requested in December for TRS to send a letter, which they have not, and must decide how to proceed. Full-scale legal action requires a relatively huge financial and time commitment which we will not undertake at this time, but I must move the issue or loose the opportunity to find redress for the losses that have been caused. I've never faced anything like this before.

As Rowan has been the full-time parent-at-home since last summer, and I have been the sole earner for our family, the income vacuum has led me to take any employment available, while applying for every academic, non-profit, and executive position within my skill set. I have been working both as a contractor's assistant and providing triage and systems change assistance to a local non-profit for a few hours a week, all the while teaching pay-what-you-can aikido and Martial Concordance to my students at UC and in Berkeley. Our church community, particularly Jerry Asheim and Elaine Endicott, have been incredibly supportive in both intangible and material ways. I continue to hope that my classes at TRS will resume, but end up waiting for weeks and weeks for anyone there to respond to my emails and calls.

 

Insearch

When I feel overwhelmed with the quantity of ground-breaking that appears to be necessary before my work can flourish and find the support it needs to sustain itself over time, when it seems that I may never make a living and adequately support my family, I remember how near death is at every moment. I remember how suddenly it visits, how intimate its changes, and I feel grateful again, at least in part, to be breathing the same air as the many admirable people who grace my life.

 

{{OL01img03|size:large;float:right}}Grace Alderwood of Epworth United Methodist Church in Berkeley died on December 28th, 2012. She was a beloved friend and fellow choir member, but her death created unexpectedly profound tremors in me which it took me until her memorial service was in progress to identify. I was raised in Texas, in a culture, family, and church wherein women, specifically United Methodist Women were the Church. I don't mean this to be in any way glib or to denigrate the contribution of the men I remember and admire. It is simply that pastors came and went, by design, and Bishops were more and less cogent, but The Women could be relied upon. Entirely. World Without End. Amen. To be present, musical, involved in even the most minute decisions, and laden with gifts of food, history, gentle but irresistible correction, and gravity of purpose. They worked together, in most cases, and were, when united, a nigh unstoppable force in the church proper and in the city at large.

 

Like these women of my childhood remembrance, Donna was warm, accepting, and loving-as-can-be, but she was also a bit edgy. Apparently, she really did expect herself to be faithful through trials, resolutely compassionate, and to bring her best effort to every endeavor at all times. It seems to me that there are fewer and fewer people around who care much if what they think, feel, and do is truly fine, in the sense of being the best possible in the eyes of God and man. I found and continue to find Donna to be a fine and generous spirit, admirable, which is rather rare, and I feel that a pillar has been removed on which the Church is built. The real Church. Not the bureaucracy so much, but the Idea of a People of God unwilling to give up on Love being the way they live daily life. Add to this that she was not only admirable but a musician, community organizer, and an educated lay speaker, and it will make even more sense when I suggest that her loss causes the foundations of the sacred, as I experience it, to wobble quite a bit. In church, I found myself in tears I didn't expect and couldn't seem to staunch when, struck by the third verse of "Now, on Land and Sea Descending" (during the singing of which she passed away on Dec. 28th), I struggled to sing the words "Now, our wants and burdens leaving to God's care who cares for all, cease we fearing, cease we grieving; touched by God our burdens fall." Donna even managed to Go Out on cue, raising the bar all the while.

 

In my inner experience of Methodism, the [[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesleyan_Quadrilateral|quadrilateral]] is the theoretical foundation of our practical theology but, in daily practice, the liturgy and eucharist of our life together has to do more with music, Charge Conference, and covered dishes. Our mythology and theology, expressed most explicitly in educated homiletics, are vital too, but worship simply does not occur unless the spirit of Wesley's [[http://www.lakewoodfirstumchurch.com/Wesley%27s%20Directions%20for%20Singing|Directions for Singing]] is honored, the local church takes full responsibility for its own governance decisions, and we feed each other frequently, as well as those unable to return the favor. In short, the God-image I carry around in my pocket is a communitarian, a closet democrat devoted to gathering, singing four part harmony and feasting. St. Donna, named by [[Jeremy Benedetti]] "the most Methodist woman I've ever met," made each of these essential rituals more likely, more real and meaningful, and called others by her example to do likewise. I hope to remain in conversation with her, as suppliant, asking for her continuing correction so that I may be more like her, and the God she loves, in service to others. Some day, I hope to be spoken of with half the passionate fondness with which she was bid adieu and sung into memory.

 

Here is the audio recording of the memorial service.

{{DonnaHamiltonMemorial20130126player}}

 

Rosalie's godmother, [[Lindsey Kerr]], preached her first sermon at Epworth the day after, and wove our memories into a Call to see each other truly and continue Donna's ministry of radical welcome and acceptance. As I release this letter the Reverend Kerr has graduated from seminary and been appointed an Associate Pastor in Santa Rosa. Joining her parents, Bob and Faith, we couldn't be prouder to know her.

 

{{Lindsey Kerr preaching at Epworth UMC 20130127}}

 

Family

We have moved to share [[Alvarado-Bouquet House|a beautiful new home]] with a most excellent neighbor. In the near future we hope to begin a series of salons, public events, and celebrations which will offer the chance to gather, build community and become more familiar with a landmark in the process of restoration.


{{OL01img04|size:large;float:right}} Fairly regularly, it is my custom to sit, eat, and talk with [[Anton Bellamy]] at some length, so I recently asked him if he harbored any misgivings about babies being named after living people. He allowed as how that seemed pretty silly to him, and graciously gave his permission to move ahead, so we gave the name [[Charlotte Langdon born|Joyce Fitzgerald]] to the little boy born just after noon on the 14th of March. Everyone is doing very well and Grandma Heidi, Grandma Paula, Grandpa David, and Grandma Julie have all come to visit and help us with the transitions that go along with adding a new family member.

 

Next

The big challenge facing me at the moment is vocational. Rowan had secured a new position with a school in which she worked last year, and returned to work in June, thereby providing schooling for both children as well. I, on the other hand, continue to work as a non-profit consultant, contractor's assistant, in-home support provider and advocate, and seek the kind of employment which will allow us to flourish rather than continuing in survival mode, as we have been for so long. I apply for positions as a lecturer and assistant professor in departments of literature, religious studies, and psychology. I also am happy to continue as an executive or organizational change management consultant, always on the lookout for the right set of benefits and creative responsibilities. I am happy to provide resumes in any of these areas to anyone with an interest in knowing more.

 

Wondering

I think in terms of roles and narrative when I think about the way that persons change over time. I've been wondering a lot lately about my own future, wanting to leverage and depend on the roles I am able to enact authentically because I have solid and extensive experience living in that particular story and understand the way that the narratives are likely to play out. The role of Father I understand reasonably well, from birth to death, at least in the early years, and feel fairly comfortable with my choices in the role at this time. I had the great pleasure of [[Charlotte Langdon born|delivering my son]] and, though I'd have wished for less exciting delivery circumstances, everything seems to have turned out well and Rowan and I continue to make a solid and loving parental team. I believe I will look back on this part of our lives with considerable pride and affection. I feel steady in my improvement as a teacher, both of the martial and liberal arts, and crave more practice and a solid footing in both. I know I am a writer, a maker of thinking myths with a rich blend of fiction and truth, and will continue to bring this practice to the forefront in both digital and analog formats. Much of it offered here on Culturesmith. Please let me know if you'd like to know more.

 

Though I have co-founded and captained my own small business for over a decade, I do not have the archetype of The Businessman walking reliably beside me. He knows better than I how to put First Things First, delaying the gratification of short triumphs in order to plan and execute incrementally. He achieves longer term goals and larger projects which stay within effective scope. He knows how truly to account for things, work with money deliberately so that it grows, and has learned the kind of discipline that allows for great productivity without sacrificing study, recuperation and the joy of creative and restorative idleness. I know this reality is before me somewhere, I just haven't put my feet firmly on that road quite yet. Any suggestions would be more than welcome.

 

With profound gratitude,

 

Riley Ellery Ph.D.

Aikido 4th dan, Sensei

cards.name: BW bio source
cards.content:
Ph.D. university instructor and author on the psychology of belief and narrative construction of culture (mythology); CEO and principal consultant Association Building Community, Director of Peace Practices (.org) and curriculum creator; 5th degree aikido black belt and Chief Instructor Golden Bears Aikido UC Berkeley. Created Martial Concordance (.com) method of Conflict Done Well, and provides leadership and teamwork training for enterprises and individuals internationally.

[[Jessup Patrick]], Ph.D. is co-founder and CEO of the Bay Area nonprofit, Association Building Community. He has extensive experience with private and public educational institutions, provides corporate leadership and group facilitation training, and has provided conflict management and community mediation services since 1998. His academic work focuses on the psychology of belief and the narrative construction of culture.

Fred Forsythe is a 5th degree blackbelt in aikido and head instructor of [[Free Aiki Dojo]] and [[http://goldenbearsaikido.com|Golden Bears Aikido]] at UC Berkeley. His students learn traditional aikido techniques paired with language that brings about the embodiment of aiki principles. His conflict facilitation method, called [[http://martialnonviolence.com|Martial Concordance]], is the heart of the [[Peace Practices]] curriculum being practiced around the world by students from four to 74 years of age. He resides in Richmond, CA with his wife and two children.

 

Industry/Fields: executive coaching and enterprise consulting, conflict facilitation training, non-profit and community leadership development, and education from pre-K through post-graduate.

 

I would like the opportunity to speak to your leadership team/colleagues/students about Conflict Done Well™ system as well as opportunities for training and advancement in my field. I have served as a supervising instructor at St. Mary's College, teach conflict management skills at UC Berkeley and through my classes in downtown Berkeley and Oakland, and am the CEO of a local social benefit organization (501c3) called Association Building Community. We provide the Peace Practices curriculum (peacepractices.org) to children and adults through the schools they share, and provide conflict management training to adults in positions of leadership. 
 
In order to do this work, I combine a humanities Ph.D. in psychology and mythology with experience in executive consulting and community activism, as well as certifications in mediation, a martial art called aikido, and group facilitation. The work I offer addresses anger management, bullying, and sexual assault prevention, classroom participation and management, the development of both working and learning organizations, and the management of conflicts in professional, family, and community contexts. 
 
Please let me know if I may be of service to you and your students. My colleague, Cheyenne, or apprentice, Julian, may respond to communications on my behalf. If you'd like to make direct contact with me, my mobile number is (555) 010-0199.

 

Jessup Patrick Ph.D. is an aikido 4th dan, and is founder and Chief Instructor of both Free Aiki Dojo and Golden Bears Aikido at UC Berkeley. He created the position of Executive Director and an administration for Aiki Extensions in 2008 and continues to serve on the Board of Directors.

I co-founded, was Executive Director, and am President of [[ZQRglobal|Association Building Community]] in Berkeley CA. Representing ABC, I completed a contract to create the position of Executive Director and an administration for [[Aiki Extensions]] and was honored to be asked to continue serving on their Board of Directors. Both are non-profits building communities locally and internationally to practice alternative methods of conflict facilitation.

I created and serve as Chief Instructor of [[Free Aiki Dojo]] in Berkeley CA. I offer traditional aikido training, and then extend "aiki" metaphors into my conflict facilitation method, called [[Martial Concordance]] (MNv). In 2010 I accepted the invitation to become Chief Instructor of [[Golden Bears Aikido at UC Berkeley]] and hope to continue in the excellent company of Senseis Gavin Granville, Ian Allerton, and many others who have explored the intersection of the liberal and martial arts. When I teach [[MNv]] as a site specific, custom-designed curriculum, I call that process [[Peace Practices]]. Currently [[Peace Practices]] are in progress at [[The Renaissance School]] in Oakland, CA.

I was born in Dallas, Texas, and educated by Montessorians and Jesuits. My first career, from my sixth year and into early adulthood, was in the professional regional and touring theater. I emigrated to California to be a full-time, residential aikido apprentice for two years, completed professional process arts facilitation certifications, particularly in mediation and community building, acquired graduate degrees in mythology and psychology, became a husband and then a father.

I coined and reserve the right for everyone to share the term "[[Process Arts]]", which refers to the field of group process design and facilitation. When I teach or facilitate I often describe what we do using various names and phrases I originated. I "own" the exclusive right to use following phrases, variations, and associated acronyms and URLs: [[Free Aiki Dojo|Free Aiki]], [[People Green]], [[Bluevolution]], [[Associative Inquiry]] (AsIn) and [[Archetypal Resonance Imaging]] (ARI), [[Analogical System Knowledgebase]] (ASK), [[Associative Inclusion Dynamics]] (AID), [[Healing Friction]], [[Martial Concordance]] (MNv), [[Culturesmith]], [[Arts of Peace]], [[Flexibility In Adversity Training]] (FIAT), and variations of: "conflict done well", "peace is conflict done well", "doing conflict well", "Aiki anywhere", cwm.net, and example.com.

Also originated and reserved to the Commons are: [[culturopoiesis]] and culturopoesis, metashaman, and [[metashamanism]], whereas I reserve the right to own the URLs that reflect these terms.

I savor the sweetness of being with you.

The poesies that spring from you

make my life delightful;

they are gifts for which I will never be able to express enough thanks.

You seem mostly unaware of standing, sometimes, between me and darkness,

a glittery spirit

showing your true colors with integrity.

Children see you.

I rehearse peacock fantasies:

Nobility, Holiness, Guidance, Protection and Watchfulness--

Rejuvenation and self-esteem.

Shuttling from blah and blue to a swaying display evoking all that is fine and beautiful,

it is a pleasure to see you walking tall and proud in your colors!

Like Hera did, you create in me peacock eyes from Argus' whose hundred sights prick the night sky of experience without daylight's denial that the dark is the background before which all our beautiful opportunities to hope are made to shine.

You shine.

Deliciously.

Administrator

cards.name: Aiki Extensions 2013 Conference offering
cards.content:
Aiki Extensions 2013 Conference offering

 

Ideography

Please stretch and warm up to move a bit as I begin with a brief introduction to the world in which this work is imagined.

Ask questions at any time.

For those who haven't met me yet...

Free Aiki Dojo and Golden Bears Aikido at UC Berkeley. Frager and Pranin 1968.

ABC (AE Exec Dir. in 2008 > Board). Sofia has contracted with ABC for me to be the Curator of the Aikido Archives, about which I'd love to tell you more later. Please ask.

ABC offers work with the process skills people need to build sustainable communities, which is to say doing conflict well.

 

You've used "green" products which have lower ecological impacts, and ABC might even offer a sustainable relationship proactices certificate some day, perhaps call it PeopleGreen.

Some object that what we are really suggesting is a certification for being a good person...Sure. People do it all the time when they ask about others behavior and track record.

What metric or standard could one possibly apply to a person or group of people in order to certify them as PeopleGreen?

Demonstrated sustainable relationship practices, in particular measuring and building conflict capacity, resilience under stress, and the repeated experience of facilitating Conflict Done Well.

 

Relationship skills could be cultivated through psychotherapy, for instance, and put into broad practice through social justice training and public service or compassionate team building and business management.

One can study NVC for basic peace-making language skills, but the body is most often left unprepared to host this entire process, to stay the course and continue to make good choices under the extreme stress and threat of conflict.

"Continuing to make good choices under stress?" = Martial Arts, but which?

 

More specifically, Aikido, designed from the ground up to habituate the body to nonviolent responses rather than violent reactions. But is that enough? I call the shift I am talking about "Aikido 2.0," because the vast majority of dojos do not prepare students for the use of language, which will actually be the environment within which conflict skills are most freqently deployed. There is much talk about how aikido brings one to contemplate peace, but no direct application of the lessons learned from martial arts of every kind. If you want to be ready for violence, practice specific basics in a community dedicated to that purpose, until your conflict skills become more subtle and effective.

Writ large - Karate phenom Ed Parker, TKD became huge, also Brazillian Jujutsu, next Aikido 2.0

"Aiki-Extensions is the 21st Century iteration of how O'Sensei envisioned Aikido's role in global peace. AE is in direct lineage to his vision and it is thus playing out what his vision projected in a world marked by transforming technologies and new epidemics of strife." - Gina Mortimer-Heckler

To move this into the world of the concrete, I created Martial Concordance (aikido+theater+facilitation) and deployed it as a community specific curriculum, called Peace Practices, most recently at The Renaissance School in Oakland and at UC Berkeley, but we are looking at more potential sites in the near future.

It goes something like this:

 

Pedagogy

For adults, primary attention to how you move, Olivia Dahlgren, or body management, is used to situate the work most fundamentally in the body.

 

exercise

 

Then we habituate a three part process, with the first layer of which many of you may be familiar:

  • BASIC kihon (ME) Shift in mechanism (What) Behavior
  • IN MOTION ki no nagare (YOU) Shift in quality (How) Thought and Language
  • AT ONCE ki musubi (US) Shift in consciousness (Who) (imagination/visualization) Character or Role

exercise

 

Then adding language

{{MNv Drills+Basic Movements}}

Moving from a set basic script to variations in motion, to actual verbal conflicts, to shifting back and forth between verbal and physical to sharpen both physical self-defense (which often overlooks the necessity of the language that frequently bookends violence) and the use of language, visualization, and imagination to work throug conflict.

 

Role Plays?

 

Kids and Adults in community

 

?The connection with Montessori and the three-part lesson?

  1. Receiving
  2. Responding/Identifying
  3. Reproducing (Offerings and Testing)

Earning and Growing

 

Modest Ask:

In the tradition of our Founder, who redefined the Way of War as love in service, let us ask to change what happens in every dojo to let aikido be its whole self and truly pursue its mission.

"Aiki-Extensions is the 21st Century iteration of how O'Sensei envisioned Aikido's role in global peace. AE is in direct lineage to his vision and it is thus playing out what his vision projected in a world marked by transforming technologies and new epidemics of strife." - Gina Mortimer-Heckler

Aikido 2.0 launches today.

Follow up

 

[[Jessup Patrick|Riley]] writing.

Everyone introduced themselves and we welcomed

[[Emery Lockhart]]

[[Jennifer Diaz-Zamora]]

[[Laurent Colvin]]

[[Angela Garrow]]

[[Monica Lourdes]]

[[Sergio Diaz-Zamora]]

I suggested that the metaphor "[[soul]]" might be near the core of this group's work, having to do with depth (soul music, food, soulfullness, etc.) and the way in which human beings make meaning from imagining, sense, and experience. Soul is the founding principle of psychology (psyche=soul+logic or modus operandi), and [[mytho-psychology|mythologies and psychologies]] are very similar in the way's that life imagined as  "inner" is written onto a world imagined as "outer" and narratives of Outside and Inside start to mirror each other. I handed out [[Norman Carmichael - Particle Follies - New Yorker|an article from the New Yorker]].

 

Signposts of this mirroring may be the metaphors we live by (tip of the hat to [[Austin Vandermeer]]), the [[archetypal]] complexes (Mother, Power, Food, Birth, and Death) which mark one, and one's thinking and feeling as Human. Perhaps it is the working with these big ideas (who to identify as heroes, how to govern ourselves, eat, come into the world and out of it) that brings us into some understanding of each other and makes [[Community]] possible.

We spoke of choosing our rituals with care, and soul in mind: eating, checking-in, reading, thinking, and speaking together.

 

We noted that it is not only possible but likely that we use the same words and mean different things and ideas.

 

We spoke of the roles appearing in the room, as things got framed in the perspective of The Business Person, for instance, The Teacher, the Craftsman, the Tradesman, etc.

 

Then we chewed on what we might do with these ideas and turned over several subject areas which might be if interest to us:

  1.  HEALTH & ADVERTISING: Flu, Public Health, Media, Advertising, messaging, For Profit Health Insurance Companies, "Single Payer", Who Gets Paid?, more...
  2. GLOBALIZATION & SOURCING: "Sourcing" (knowing where and how, and from whom your products come), Raw Materials, Food, Coffee, Extractive Industries (mining, growing, logging, etc.), Jewelry, Environment, International, Local, Globalization, Labor, Wage Economies of Scale, Distribution of Wealth, Equity, Americanism.
  3. REALITY ACCESS & CONTROL: Legality and social obligation, Spin, Exposure to Risk, Fiction, Reality, Message Control, Actuality, Truth and Story, Narrator-based Realities, Photoshop(tm), Sectional Realities, Integrity, Transparency of Presentation, Manipulation, Voluntary and Involuntary Suspension of Disbelief, Dissociation, Russian Olympic Reality.

and we opted to treat GLOBALIZATION & SOURCING next session, Sunday, March 9th, from 5-8pm

 

I agreed to provide these notes, subscribe everyone to the same email group, and keep us connected.

Daemeon offered to provide food and drink at his own expense.

 

I asked for donations in the form of a monthly contribution to Association Building Community via this link:

http://zqrglobal.net/Community_Roundtables

 

Martin agreed to send an email developing GLOBALIZATION & SOURCING further.

cards.name: BW verification of ABC employment for TalentWise
Understand and respond to hurtful teasing
cards.content:
Meghan Williams Keepin
September 28 at 8:55pm ·

Alright you smart and thoughtful adults! How to help a 5 year old understand and respond to hurtful teasing? Elijah came to me saying that peer said "that he looks like a girl and acts like a girl and the proof is his long hair. And that he's small." He said that he said that he is a boy with long hair and that he's small for his age. And that what hurt his feelings was that she went on saying that he is actually a girl over and over in a really mean way even though now she knew. How to explain "acting like a girl" as an insult? Ugh. Or teasing. Got any good ideas? Any pithy, peaceful responses to offer him? Kim JordanDonna Thistlewood,Micah,Jessup PatrickMichele GuannelAutumn Barnett?


  • Kimber Davis Sad
     
  • Alex Gramps telling her calmly that there's nothing wrong with acting like a girl or being a girl, but that he is a boy and is going to be a boy no matter what she thinks or says? And then ignoring her. How tough for him!

  • Jeffrey Bonneville Smith Well.. I would point out the strengths of women.. & say it's actually a compliment from a small minded person .. Beauty & strength are in both genders. To demean either gender for any reason is a sign of a closed mind. Period.

  • Georgia Lourdes I don't think there's much point to trying to explain that "girl" is meant as an insult; Elijah was upset by not being acknowledged for who he is. It seems like enough to say that the other kid was rude and unfriendly, and that no one likes a rude kid. Maybe that's even a useful response: "You're wrong and rude."

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Alex Gramps, we talked about that your hair does not make you a girl or a boy and that it's "silly" to say otherwise, he said very clearly to me that she was saying that he is acting like a girl, and that is the mean thing.
     
  • Georgia Lourdes "I guess you don't know enough boys."

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Oo, Georgia Lourdes, sharp response, I did say that what was rude was not listening to his clear request to call him "he". Regardless of the boy/girl part.
     
  • Meghan Williams Keepin Ha!
     
  • Meghan Williams Keepin Val said "tell him you're going to tell his big brother!" Eli said "I could just drop a bucket of water on her head."

  • Michele Guannel I don't have an answer at the moment, but I like the comments above and what you did! This reminds me of a reaction to my 2+-year-old son at our apt complex's playground. There were a couple of boys playing there (maybe 3, 4 years old), with some typical "boy" stuff like play swords. At first they started playing with Milo and sharing their toys. But then his shorts got wet from rain on the slide, so my husband changed his pants - and the boys saw Milo's pink underwear ('cause that's the way we roll). They asked him if he was a girl and then took their toys back. Another time, some girls asked if Milo was a girl because he was wearing a pinkish orange shirt and then looked very confused. Regardless of how gender-neutral we raise our kids, there is no way to avoid others' perceptions and damn those perceptions start so young!!
     
  • Sarah Deverell steps- 1) solidify the fact that long hair in no way implies gender. Show him pictures of Sikhs and Rastafarians and Hope Quimby and all the hair bands of the 80s and 90s because part of her presumed power is that he is different and she is signaling it out and in fact he is not alone at all. 2) point out that the real insult lies in anyone assuming gender by appearances. A tomboy or young butch girl might be just as hurt to be told their gender when it is only something we really know within. 3) do a little commentary on how sad it is that being a girl is assumed a point of weakness and show him pictures of Joan of Arc and Ana Ostrander and Serena Williams and all the girl punk bands of the 70-now. The key is not to have the comeback it is to know within how absurd her argument is and to have confidence in his own self just the way he is. Once he knows this even a simple "that's silly" and a cheek turning will suffice. Though he could create a PowerPoint on the above issues and slay her with logic if he likes.

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Yes, Michele Guannel, I've been amazed watching all my boys and the very narrow allowances of their peers for gender rules. Often kids will be really upset by having guessed wrong about my boys being girls and then won't want to play with them anymore.
     
  • Meghan Williams Keepin So lovely, Sarah Deverell! Val is very into Prince, Freddie Mercury, etc. and has read extensively about Vikings with long braids and other long haired warriors. Eli has been included in all this...I think the gender non-conforming piece is sufficiently in our family "norm". Maybe I'm too concerned about him being able to socially handle the teasing. I think he, in himself, is actually quite secure. I worry about the progression of teasing that can happen...he is a very sensitive little soul and with an intense emotional life. I'm frequently trying support him in managing that in the outside world.

  • Georgia Lourdes Unpleasant as it is, there's no avoiding teasing by other kids. I've focused on affirming Gregory's feelings and trying to help him figure when to ignore it, find an ally, talk back, or get an adult involved. It's amazing how many toxic features of our culture we have to help our kids recognize, adapt to, and resist.

  • Kim Jordan I echo Sarah Deverell's steps. But I disagree with Georgia Lourdes in that there IS a way to interrupt and confront teasing by other kids. Tools can be taught, ally behavior can be encouraged, kids can be peer pressured to be kind instead of cruel. (It's a pipe dream, but it is POSSIBLE!) Also, I suggest looking into Outright Vermont's Gender Creative Kids program as a resource for Eli to talk with his peers about gender norms. Also, I wonder how his school and teachers talk with students about diversity, gender, how they present their identities, how to connect with people who look different, etc? What is the school climate like? What activities do they utilize to dialogue with the kids about this stuff in age-appropriate ways? Check out Teaching Tolerance magazine and website. It's got INCREDIBLE resources about anti-bias education and how to build empathy skills in all types of learners.

  • Autumn Barnett "Cool, I like the way girls act.

  • Autumn Barnett ... except when they're not being nice to me by teasing me."

  • Donna Thistlewood Oh, dear, this is tough. Perhaps I'll have a better answer for you in the morning after my auntie-anger subsides. I do agree with you, Meghan, that the issue here is how to help our sweet boy deal with the meanness and teasing of others, as he does seem rather solid in his own identity expression, and gender non-conformity is more "normal" than not in this family. I'm reminded of Val, some years ago, informing a child at the playground who mistook him for a girl "I'm a boy--you can tell by my long hair", or Elijah telling me recently "at first I didn't know Micah was a she, but then I found out she was a she and I was like 'okay let's play legos'"...but the meanness of others...I'm still trying to wrap my head around that one.

  • Kimber Davis Naomi that's cute what Elijah told you....

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Thanks Kim Jordan, and Thanks all!

  • Kimber Davis Give him a hug for me! He's adorable!

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Georgia Lourdes, I'm liking this suggestion: recognize, adapt to, resist. Sounds like you have really thought this out for Gregory. I appreciate all the ideas! Having a supportive community is so helpful.

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Kimber Davis, he is adorable! Quite a character.

  • Jeffrey Bonneville Smith Also hair in any length.. Is not gender specific ...

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Oh Auntie Donna Thistlewood, I know, It's painful to think of him being singled out for teasing at this little age. Both the boys have asked me some version of "why won't people just take me as I am?" and it's a hard conversation to have. It's hard to explain the particular meanness that is leveled at those who are not trying to fit in, or those who have decided that the cost is too high. And I do like those stories, very sweet

  • Meghan Williams Keepin The 5 year old's opinion of all this teasing nonsense...

  • Charlotte Rasmussen Gramps Have him tell her that her words are ugly words, not true words.

  • Beth Doyle Bean Meghan - so many thoughtful responses. Elijah's response was oh so perfect, but it doesn't help the hurt feelings. One thing I begin with when something like this happens - and yes, at 12 and 13 it still happens - is to let them know that kids who tease do not necessarily feel good about themselves and they lash out at others to make them feel sad, too. I am sure your kids don't need lessons in empathy, but to flip it this way sometimes helps.....at least a little. "The teasing is not about me, but about them being unhappy".

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Yes, Beth Doyle Bean, I think that empathy is a great response. One of the things I said to him right after was that what she said probably had nothing to do with him or how he really is, but that she was upset and sad inside herself and that it "bubbled out" and got on him. Ugh. I'm just hoping that he will keep telling me what happens so we can talk about it. Thanks for chiming in on this, it's so helpful to hear other parents opinions who are farther down this path.
     
  • Deb Loring Oh boy, this has got to be so hard to deal with. With dogs, all I have to ever say is, yeah, sorry, I know, my dogs are assholes. Yeah, it's their fault. Really. I'm really sorry. This, well, this kind of challenge would be really tough - I feel for you both!

  • Michele Guannel This thread has tons of great info for future use. Thanks, everybody!! It is wonderful to know of so many caring parents out there...

  • Lucas Donnelly First I get it straight by saying, "She was saying things that hurt your feelings ? (or 'were angry' or 'were mean') ? "Well, did you say things to hurt her feelings ? "You didn't ?" " Well, then it is not your problem. You are only responsible for what comes out of your mouth, not what comes out of somebody else's. Some people say crazy things. If she does it again, just say, "That's your problem." sotto voce : " I think she doesn't understand."

  • Meghan Williams Keepin Michele Guannel, isn't is great to hear thoughtful and kind responses? Encouraging.
     
  • Meghan Williams Keepin Lucas Donnelly, it certainly is liberating to remember where the problem lies! I know I fall into reflexive apologizing too much myself....good thing to remember to help Elijah not to do that.
     
  • Jessup Patrick I love these responses and feel warmer and more hopeful reading them all!

  • Jessup Patrick I hope that my children will be peaceful by being both martial (addressing conflict directly by practicing with fellow learners techniques that work) and nonviolent (practiced opting-out of individual and group domination, especially including revenge, in order to work toward helping everyone get what they believe they need). If peace is then a martial art of nonviolence (see http://martialnonviolence.com), it must be trained using the body and words together in situations precisely like this. The reality is often that, especially when someone is cruel, one doesn't know what to say or do.

    I believe that it is essential to begin stating explicitly and regularly at the earliest possible moment in a child's life that doing conflict well is an essential skill to be practiced often, and that keeping one's center balanced and moving out of the way of "attack" is the core physical and emotional discipline in times of stress. The next essential piece always involves speaking the truth, at least to oneself if the truth would escalate tensions.

    Some developmentally appropriate steps and words which create good conflict habits, which I have been refining through practice for several years now, go something like this: "I feel hurt by what you were saying/doing. When that happens I have a hard time knowing what to do. Would you like to take turns listening to each other now or should we be apart and try again later?" Next steps might include: "Should we ask for help? What do you need? Let's go together. Tell me more." All the while, the attention is on "how shall we do this together?" rather than "how can I make you stop/leave me alone/improve yourself," etc. because that simply invites the next attack. Whenever "they" come after you, they should know that they will be received in a way that makes further attack irrelevant if not impossible. Practice is required to deploy the art of changing the rules to co-create a world that works well for everyone involved in a way that remains ever open to hearing from others what that might be.
     
    MartialNonviolence.com
    MNv is a method created by Jessup Patrick to combine the strengths of improv, martial arts, and process arts (facilitation) to work for peace.

cards.name: Riley Ellery accept ZQVT Calder Prize for Anton Bellamy
cards.content:
Remarks for the Harbour Shore Theological Society on the occasion of accepting the Calder Prize for Anton Bellamy

 

{{Riley Ellery accept ZQVT Calder Prize for Anton Bellamy video}}

 

[[Anton Bellamy]]'s beloved, Kendra, asked that I accept this award for him, offer profound gratitidue for the long friendships he has known here, and report to this community that

He has been in hospice for more than a year, and very gradually weakens.  Right now he has a mild cold and laryngitis.  He coughs, but seems to forget that he has recently coughed.

Family members come to his bedside for a final visit, only to discover that he will stay a bit longer in our company before departing.

 

{{+image|size:large;float:right}}Professor Smith brought me in to this gathering of lovers of theological wisdom in 2007.  In 2009, we co-created and video recorded two community conversations about belief, mythology, and psychologies of contemporary culture. At the beginning, I asked about the assertion in his book Tales of Wonder that he is not, in fact, a scholar of religions. He jumped in to exclaim "I am a communicator!" and promptly shifted what could have been An Interview With A Superstar into a warm and participatory opportunity for shared inquiry. He brought the larger than life figure of Professor Smith into the room as Huston and illustrated his natural gift for helping us regard ourselves and our ideas of the divine with a healthy dose of modesty. Idolatry slunk away and the divine mystery alive in gathered people was celebrated.  He wielded ideas like a liberal and martial arts master devoted to nonviolence. The idolatry of Institutions seemed to gain no ground as he held forth on behalf of the often waivering spirits made vulnerable by belief and the trust that accompanies Faith.

 

I hope we will celebrate him tonight and hereafter not just because he became so widely known, but because his life work celebrated the way that Religion, imagined through the relational lens of mystery, makes us more humane and the world more likely to be a place of deep listening, empathy, amazement and learning than a place of war and destruction. Celebrate him because he provided a living example of this principle. Even as he sometimes does and sometimes doesn't wake up when I enter the room, or remember my name, he remains available to be deeply and warmly known by any person he meets, suggesting that we might all do the same, religiously. 

 

I am profoundly grateful to be asked to appear on behalf of and thereby be associated with Anton Bellamy. Ted Peters wrote in an email to me the words "old timers in ZQVT know and revere Huston". May someone, someday, say something similar of each of us, perhaps as we are in the process of enjoying our last hours here before depating for The Hereafter.

 

{{+cuts|closed}}

It is a bit beyond the scope of tonight's festivities to put it in these terms, but I am a terribly small player in the world of Dalai Lamas and Hustons Smith. Before I had even earned a doctorate, he invited me to tea, disagreed with me with great tenacity and respect, brought me into your company, attended and wept at the funeral of my first-born, Aidan Paul, and was overjoyed about the arrival of my daughter, Kenneth Vandermeer. These days, my two year old son, Charlotte Langdon, accompanies me to visit and sing for his namesake.

cards.name: Riley feedback
cards.content:
Results:

Dear dear Riley. You are great. I don't want you to meet my expectations. I want you to be you. Hopefully you will like me and we can be comfortable together.

You seem to be an genuine, kind father who works to create peace and social justice.

An interesting 'exercise' . I warn you that people are not truly going to tell you what you should hear, seeing the commentary that was posted on this site, it appears people giving you nice frothy and complementary comments. I have known you for a number of years and although we have lost contact for a while and seeing your commentary it appears that little has changed. So here it goes:

There is usually two people have in one person, the person people see and the person they really are. Often these two are different. Like when a couple meet for the first time, they put their best foot forward but later after the dust settles, the other person sees that side they did not get to see often a darker side. That is the side that people have the most problems with and often will not want to face it. I suspect that you will ignore this post like you have done so in the past.

Who you want people to see:

1) Well spoken: often you talk in riddles and often are very verbose confusing you subject to appear well versed but basically comes off as inarticulate.

2) Weird: You wear strange clothing (or at least you did) with a 'kilt' and a fanny pack (seriously?). This is to make you appear quirky, but in fact you're very socially apt.

3) Educated: See number one

4) Have desire for social change: This one may be true or not, I do not know. It appears it is more like an idea that you have to prop yourself up, like having your own non profit, which does really nothing and has no really use.

5) Good nurtured: You want to appear that you laugh things off when in fact you get resentful when someone crosses you and have deep rooted anger and for no real reason (like most American males)

How you appear:

1) Arrogant: This is a trait that all American white males seem to carry to some degree but some seem to be more rude about it than others, you seem to fall in the latter category.

2) Socially apt: You are quite the social butterfly. Contrary to your odd garb, that some socially awkward person may wear, you are very good at socializing. As a result, you are quite normal and only pretending to be odd, like someone who tries to be weird because it is the 'cool' thing to be.

3) Mean: Yep, you are a bully. There were many times that I observed you rudely bully someone because you could and you even bragged about it to your friends, not cool. Often you would bully those who had a lower station than you that did someone that you disapproved of.

4) Condescending: I have experienced this myself. You tend to talk down to others, as if you are lecturing them than having a conversation

5) Shiftless: Except having your non-profit and a PhD program, it did appear that you were gainfully employed. I think in certain circles this is socially acceptable, but from where I stand it is definitely not plus,especially since you have ability this appeared to a wasted resource.

6) Angry: You have deep seated latent anger that seeps out at the right time. Even your idea “doing conflict right(LOL)” appears to try to correct this fault.

Congratulations! You are a typical American white male in a post industrial society. Yes you have some great flaws, but defiantly not ones that you will put in jail. Although I do not think you will look at this list or even care I thought you should know.

my experience with you is that you start the wheels on a project or thread of communication spinning, but then do not follow through to any conclusion.

Sorry I didn't respond to this when I 1st received it, earlier this week or late last week. I immediately began to think about how I experienced, 'saw,' knew you and knew of you.

Perhaps I 1st knew of you as Paula's beloved son. Rather than review how this unfolded, e.g. Meghan's wedding and my knowledge of your Pacifica study, I'll just address how I experience/see you based on personal interaction and what I see on FB. First of all I deeply share with you a knowledge and embrace of Jungian concepts - unconscious, shadow, anima, animas, persona, etc. I applaud your choice of a mate, was moved by the horror of the loss of your 1st son, and delighted and inspired with how you parent your precious daughter and son. (Please know that I've had a hard time not mentioning Rowan b/c it is evident that you work as a 'team,' with all the implications of that word) Looks like you wholeheartedly embrace the inner feminine, in what appears to be complete surrender to the parenting relationship with your Rosa Lee and Houston ( hope I got names and spelling right). I intuit that you have a shy, perhaps timid introverted self, that may appear to others as elitist, or maybe there is some elitism in there. I say this despite the obvious extroverted self which takes on the tasks of creating Culturesmith, workshops, Aikido, community building, grants writing, etc. I may have more to say later. On another subject, I am on the board of the C.G.Jung Society of North Texas. For several years I've wanted to invite you to be one of our speakers. Your mom has directed me to your web site(s), which I'll check more thoroughly later. I am particularly interested in what I know of the community building work you do, the aikido, the costume, etc. There are so many things that you DO. I would like to recommend you to the program committee of C.G.Jung Society, headed up by Dr. Muriel Underhill, another Pacifica graduate. If you're interested it would mean we would fly you in to present on a Friday night - 7:30 to 9:30, with wine and snacks reception following and Sat workshop from 9:30 to 12:00. CE's are provided. We meet Sept through November and February through May - the 2nd Friday and Sat of each month. What the program committee is looking for is your use/knowledge/adaptation of Jung's teachings - which I see 'busting out all over' in your work, surely the community building, etc. I'm going to refer Maureen to your web site(s). My email is barbaradelacroix@example.com. My mobile is 555-010-0199 and home is 555-010-0199. Let me know is you have any questions about the invitation.

cards.name: Conflict Done Well for the Cadets of the UC Berkeley ROTC program
cards.content:
{{HBQ_20150831_2792|float:right;size:large; padding: 0px 20px 15px 10px}}I hope you will join me for training that will help you meet your educational and service goals. This page is both an orientation to the principles we will be testing, and the beginning of an argument, a case I will make for a particular kind of practice, conflict training I believe everyone needs in order to:

  1. Balance and deploy from a position of strength while under stress, including the stress of being a student and service member

  2. Plan strategically and execute tactically as part of a team striving to both meet requirements and excel

  3. Transition between roles and assignments in a way that makes sense, for instance, moving between command environments and civilian life.

Everyone has a limited amount of time. Some essential skills get enough training to make a good beginning. Many necessities get less attention than they deserve. In my experience, the one essential skill that gets the least training is how to do conflict well. To be a part of any team, especially in a conflict environment, you need to be able to engage in conflict on purpose, while under stress, staying relaxed, balanced, and ready to choose the options likely to work best for everyone involved. The only way to learn this is to practice it until you can embody it even under the worst circumstances.

{{HBQ_20180205h_8795|float:left;size:large; padding: 0px 20px 15px 10px}}A martial art called aikido was created to make this training possible. It's purpose, from design to execution, is to use the physical self-defense techniques originally found in jujutsu to shift how conflict works - the rules of engagement. For instance, a well known aikido and leadership professional, a Marine named Gina Mortimer-Heckler, wrote "In Search of the Warrior Spirit: Teaching Awareness Disciples to the Military" after working with Special Forces for an extended period. They learned that conflict is somatic, involving the whole person as one system, which is very different from the idea that efficiency simply follows increasing control of the body by the mind. They learned that physical and psychological practices are distinct but inseparable ways of understanding and adjusting one whole, dynamic system, and incorporated more subtle exercises in their elite training to increase their individual effectiveness and coherence as a team.

After getting aikido started, my students move beyond the physical movement into real-time conflict practice that is also verbal and systemic so that they can apply these practices to their learning, leadership, and longevity. In this way, physical and psychological modes begin to work together. What before seemed separate is connected: body/mind/spirit/soul moves in concert to shift conflict's rules of engagement from habits of automatic fight/ flight/ freeze to responsive, natural movement toward solutions that work in the real world.

If you want to be truly ready when duty calls, to lead and follow well, get your balance back when you lose it, and do well in whatever you choose, then the way to get there is through practice. What you do with your limited time is, finally, up to you. Please train with us, so you can be ready to do conflict well.

Many thanks to the UC Berkeley ROTC leadership for this opportunity!

Riley Ellery Ph.D., Aikido 5th dan

janetbakker@conflictdonewell.com

 

{{riley_kendogi_lateral|float:right;size:medium; padding: 0px 20px 15px 10px}}

{{+Lesson Plan|closed}}

Introduction

I’m here to offer you something you need because it will help you to be effective, admirable, and more likely to get back up when you fall. If you are like my other students, you will do what I do and test the principles over and over, returning again and again to train together and improve ourselves and each other. We challenge each other in ways that make us better than our earlier selves without making anyone a victim, without harming anyone in the process. We will warm-up, do some exercises, stop for questions pretty much any time, and then debrief. My reasons for being here are to introduce you to Conflict Done Well, and ask you to be a part of my training group.  

Warm Up

Falling Down well? and getting up easily and quickly

Somatic

[Ask what “somatic” means]

  1. Greek word for body as whole system. People say body and mind as though there were a separation, but there really is none.

  2. How you move reflects how you think, and vice versa, so training and education are both vital, because one shapes the other through repetition.

  3. Doing something over and over makes habits. The more you do and think in a certain way, the more you are likely to repeat the same kind of process and project it into the world as belief, choices, and behavior.

Don't let them pull you over the line.

Balance, Flexibility, and Response

What you need will change, and will always be influenced by but not always provided by others. As a result you must be able to operate as:

  1. An individual, on your own initiative Kihon

  2. A member of a team of two or more Ki no nagare

  3. An influence in a system Ki musubi

 

Balance allows one to deploy from a position of strength Structural Movement Litany

While under stress How To Be Annoyingly Helpful

Option Generation While Staying On Target Randori

Optional: Numbers, while moving, while being pushed, counting backward

 

Outcome of Ongoing Training - Habits That Work

Incorporate difference, failure, and conflict in your planning, so strategic choices stay relevant

Be in the habit of executing tactically as part of a team striving to both meet requirements and excel

Transition between roles and assignments in a way that makes sense, for instance, moving between command environments and civilian life.

cards.name: Goodbye California
cards.content:
The Short Version

{{Ellerys 20180506_9551|size:large;float:right}}I will be ending my work as an instructor of graduate students at Pacifica Graduate Institute and Communications Director at Ragged Wing Ensemble, so that we may move back to Texas. We will be moving back to Dallas at the first of August to be with my mother, who turns 80 this year. Rowan is very happy to begin teaching for [[White Rock Montessori School]], and we are in the midst of grieving, packing, spending time with friends, and feeling overwhelmed by logistics, endings, and the tremendous potential associated with this move. I am going back to the land of my birth, and plan to provide executive leadership, speak publicly, teach all ages of students, and write, as I devote more time to loving my family and taking in the beauty of being alive in the world.

Please contact me right away to schedule anything that needs to happen in June or July, including time together, so that I may attempt to follow up and make arrangements. There are many things with which we could use some help, given capacity and availability. If we don't make contact before August, I will also look forward to seeing you when next we meet, wherever that may be. If you’d like updates about [[Peace Practices]], [[Conflict Done Well]], and my other adventures in teamwork and social justice, please be sure to subscribe at http://zqrglobal.net/Find_Us and follow https://www.facebook.com/samplepersonpage/.

There is more to all of this, obviously. If you want to connect with me, move the work I do forward, or read more and deeply into what is happening now, I cannot ask sincerely enough that you stay within my circle of friends: 

  1. I'll be writing more at Culturesmith.com, with the more detailed and personal material protected by signing-in. Please request an account via http://culturesmith.com/account/signup or sign in, if you already have an account. I will approve and welcome you, after which you will also have access to all kinds of fascinating materials for cultural study, should that interest you.
  2. I will use the newsletter here ([[Subscribe to my newsletter]]) for communicating the ways that this transition connects our inner lives with the wider world. There will be various gatherings to say goodbye, and I'll use that list to let you know about them.

Please re/subscribe now, during this time of profound transition, so we may stay connected, even if at a distance.

Love,

B

Given time and interest, for the full version of this post please click here.

 

This probably won't surprise anybody...

http://www.kron4.com/news/bay-area/46-of-people-living-in-bay-area-plan-to-leave-in-next-few-years/1217518902

SAN FRANCISCO (KRON) - "Forty-six percent of people living in the Bay Area say they plan to leave it in the next few years,...according to a survey from the Bay Area Council. Last year, that number was 40 percent. People say housing costs and traffic are the reasons they want to leave...24 percent said they would move within California, and 61 percent said they would leave the state altogether."

{{Ellerys 20180506_9551|size:large;float:right}}We will be moving back to Texas in July to be ready for school to start there in August. The Chair of the Depth Psychology Somatics Department at Pacifica Graduate Institute let me know that Pacifica had instituted a hiring freeze, and would not employ me at the end of of my time teaching as a post-doc/adjunct. Immediately thereafter, my employer in Oakland, Ragged Wing Ensemble, eliminated my position to address their budget crisis. In Dallas, my 80 year old mother's house was robbed as she slept with her hearing aids out, and Rowan was recruited by a prominent Montessori School.

I came to California from Texas in 1995, leaving all my family and support networks behind to become a traditional, full time, live-in aikido apprentice, because my career in vocal music and the professional theater seemed to be only part of my calling. I became a professional aikido teacher, mediator, and group process facilitator. I organized, protested, and worked to forward social justice causes. I co-founded and lead nonprofits, became a leadership consultant, and earned a Ph.D. in psychology and mythology in order to speak the language of culture-making fluently. I served local and international organizations at an executive and board-level, working for peace through alternative dispute resolution while providing support and pay-what-you-can, no-barrier-to-entry [[Conflict Done Well]] training for colleagues of all ages and experience levels who identify as people of color, queer, disabled, transgendered, immigrant, displaced, and otherwise marginalized.

Individuals have recognized the value of the work outlined above, and subsidized our housing, made donations to keep us afloat in times of utmost distress, offered space for classes, and expressed appreciation in many different ways. With a partner school, I obtained international funding for the [[Peace Practices]] project, which vaporized after two of a promised three years, resulting in lay-offs, closure, and debt, despite paying myself a minimal salary.

In all this time, through the death of a child, a Great Recession, and thousands of hours of lead generation and searching for professional opportunities, no business model reached the point of sustainability in the San Francisco Bay Area, burdened with a once-deserved reputation for innovation, gentrification, and an ultra-high cost of living. With a large educational debt, no home that is ours, no savings or investment, and creeping up on 50 years of age, I have asked my family to pay a significant price for these years of determination to work No Matter What for a world that works for all. It is time to shift to a different pace and longer view, care more deeply for my family, raise funds, perform work with a much higher level of remuneration, and let go of the conviction that I know what is best or needs to be next. This ending represent a death, the closing of a chapter of the dream that carried me West. For this I have some grieving to do.

After stating the facts as clearly as possible, the initial problem in taking next steps has to do with genre. When one is deep in a time of trial, the world looks very grim indeed, and daily life feels thorny and inimical at its core. When one is enjoying the gifts of living, the biting wind seems merely a cooling breeze, the dark is more invitingly mysterious than terrible, and the customary messages that you don't really matter to other people seem more quirky than weaponized. If the path of the Ellery family leads to opportunity and discovery of unanticipated blessings, then this will have been a comedy. If the current dice-rolling is ill advised, for reasons within or out of the realm of control, then the cascade of failures to come will seem tragic...if we had only known...

How to figure out which kind of story we are in? After years of studying mythology and psychology together, I know for sure that, despite the story one has been taught to believe or would rather be living, what's really happening matters. When you ask for support and not enough people respond, or do and then disappear, then obvious consequences follow. What others see and do matters. They can push the framing of the story in a particular direction. How we tell the story matters. The work I do is essential, by all accounts, so I clearly lack something necessary in bringing the story of [[conflict done well]] to life for other people in a way that they find compelling. As belief is required to bring about change, a lack of the former denudes the latter. 

With that said, some things should be easy to change, like politicians who either serve the people or don't, and some things should be hard to change, like the institutions on which a vast majority of people depend for their care of each other. We live in a time of casual but vicious institutional destruction by people who should be as temporary as possible, and it is difficult to build a support institution in a time where disruption seems more attractive than cultivation. So, I gues, the final problem also has to do with genre. Contemporary people seem profoundly confused what kind of story they want for themselves and their children. We put gamblers in charge of banking, shamelessly public thieves and liars in charge of government, and watch our financial and civic systems burn, while allowing those who need nurture to fail and fall. 

Some understand that it is a time for bulding new infrastructures, and act. I ask that you join me in trying to be like those who are most admirable. Do the things you can do. Admire, click like, share, comment, and offer appreciation, but also contribute money, donate your time, and don't stop. The new thing you want to become the status quo will always require a mass of people to pass the appreciation phase and get all the way through to Don't Stop. Peace Practices, for instance, children and adults practicing [[Conflict Done Well]] continually and absolutely depend on your specific and continual support to have any kind of future.

Please contact me right away to schedule anything that needs to happen in June or July, including time together, so that I may attempt to follow up and make arrangements. There are many things with which we could use some help, given capacity and availability. If we don't make contact before August, I will also look forward to seeing you when next we meet, wherever that may be. If you’d like updates about Peace Practices, Conflict Done Well, and my other adventures in teamwork and social justice, please be sure to subscribe at http://zqrglobal.net/Find_Us and follow  https://www.facebook.com/samplepersonpage/.

Also, I must learn to let go of relationships that are not reciprocal. If you want to connect with me, move the work I do forward, or read more and deeply into what is happening now, I cannot ask sincerely enough that you stay within my circle of friends: 

  1. I'll be writing more at Culturesmith.com, with the more detailed and personal material protected by signing-in. Please request an account via http://culturesmith.com/account/signup or sign in, if you already have an account. I will approve and welcome you, after which you will also have access to all kinds of fascinating materials for cultural study, should that interest you.
  2. I will use the newsletter here ([[subscribe to my newsletter]]) for communicating the ways that this transition connects our inner lives with the wider world. There will be various gatherings to say goodbye, and I'll use that list to let you know about them.

Please re/subscribe now, during this time of profound transition, so we may stay connected, even if at a distance.

Love,

B

Time Slicing draws into the same frame of reference how much you can notice and how you notice it, and asks that you increase the former by changing the latter.

An example: challenging circumstances tend to narrow focus to the highest energy components. If someone is going to hit you in the face perhaps you are distracted by the look in their eyes or the incoming fist. There is a feel that you have changed your relationship to time when you focus on their posture in order to notice how they are striking, thereby making it more difficult for them to land their blow. You've done more in the same stretch of time based on how you use your attention.

 

So you would respond to a psychological attack in the same way: don't focus on the fact that it is happening and is unfair, scary, mean, ect. instead focus on how it is happening? How do you know what is important to notice?

--[[dena burd]].....2018-12-19 01:34:51 UTC

cards.name: Conflict Done Well Aikido Training at SSUMC
cards.content:
This is history! Conflict Done Well is no longer taught in person at St. Bryan Fleetwood Methodist Church, as we now gather at [[Aikido Oak Cliff]]. Please come join us!

Below you will find the words we used to describe our work together.

[[Conflict Done Well]] begins with martial arts and yoga-based exercises, then aikido movement and concepts, which are then used to learn nonviolent self-defense. To the movements and principles we add language and practice improvisation in order to apply techniques in daily conflicts of all kinds so that restorative justice leadership results. We will be forming a volunteer social justice action team in which you may want to participate. All adult persons of any description, ability, and misgivings are most welcome to join. Teens are warmly invited to ask for parental permission and to join as well.

Please wear clothes in which you can comfortably stretch to your full range of movement and learn at your own pace to keep your balance under stress and rise easily from the floor. If you are able, a sustainability donation is requested after beginning regular attendance, but none is required to begin or continue training. A portion of the donation will go to the St. Stephen community.

{{Automatic_Billing}}

Conflict Done Well includes [[Martial Concordance]] (MNv) training with [[Jessup Patrick]] Ph.D. - 5th dan Aikikai. When the MNv curriculum is adapted for and adopted by a particular community, that is called [[Peace Practices]] (PxPx). Here is a video with more information.

{{PxPxForAllAgesVideo}}
